wayback._eras_note: visionaries.vc belonged to a Japanese Toastmasters club (Visionaries Toastmasters Club, Musashi-Kosugi) until 2019; every capture before 2020 is that club and is not read. The firm's own site has four generations, none of which fits a generic era parser: a 2020 placeholder, a Gatsby build 2020-2022 that carried no portfolio list at all (page-data.json holds no query data; the page component bundle, fetched from the Internet Archive on 2026-09-30, has the manifesto text and a 'See portfolio' button linking to the firm's Crunchbase page), WordPress 2023-2025 (/portfolio/ with per-company /portfolio/<slug>/ posts, portfolio-sitemap.xml) and the Kirby single page of 2026 (read live through site_api). scratch/archive-parse.py reads the captures (Internet Archive and Common Crawl) and writes sources/wayback/parsed/<year>.json in wayback-pull's shape, every row carrying its exact capture_url (COLLECTION.md s1: a capture URL is a valid citation).

roster._note: The roster is curated (sources/wayback/partner-roster.json) from the live team section (sources/site/team-cards.json), the archived team sections of the Gatsby and WordPress sites, the Form D related persons of the three US-filing vehicles (Robert Lacher, Sebastian Pollok) and the firm's own promotion posts, each person with a dated basis.

site_api._entry_stage_note: The live Kirby page publishes no round, year or fund per company, so there is no field to score or promote (COLLECTION.md s5).
site_api._note: visionaries.vc (2026) is Kirby CMS; the portfolio ships server-rendered in the single page (59 companies, read 2026-09-30 by scratch/site-live.py). tomorrow.vc is VISIONARIES TOMORROW, the firm's industrial deep-tech fund (Visionaries Club Tomorrow Fund I GmbH & Co. KG, on the same ADV); its Svelte homepage lists 10 companies in the 'Change Makers' carousel (scratch/site-tomorrow.py). Earlier tomorrow.vc captures render only the carousel's first slide ('01 / 04' in 2024, '01 / 08' in 2025), so the live ten are the list.
